newsitem.title: CHINA: China sets tax for foreign bank local business.
newsitem.headline: China sets tax for foreign bank local business.

text.p: Foreign banks doing Chinese yuan business will be taxed at 15 percent but will only be allowed to seek clients from among foreign-funded firms registered in Shanghai, the official Xinhua news agency said on Tuesday.

Foreign bankers expressed surprise at the 15 percent rate, which is the same rate at which their foreign currency business is taxed, and much lower than the rate applying to Chinese banks doing the same business with the same clients.
The central bank on Monday named four foreign banks with branches in Shanghai which will be allowed to start doing local currency loans and deposits, ending months of speculation.
"Their clients can only be foreign-funded enterprises registered in the city, and they should open RMB (local currency) accounts in the central bank's Shanghai branch," Xinhua said.

"But their income tax rate will remain the same, 15 percent as before, and the central bank's Shanghai branch will provide training programs for employees of the foreign banks in RMB business dealings," it added.
"It sounds too good to be true," said a banker with one of the four foreign banks chosen to begin local currency business.
"It's especially strange because many foreign bankers have at least implied that they would be willing to accept a higher tax rate. It's very surprising," the banker added.
